_comment: Reusable scene-tuple templates for trajectory authoring. Each snippet fixes 5-6 of the 11 dim slots (the constants that define the scene type) and lists the slots the author must supply per use (the variables that distinguish one instance from another). Token IDs are drawn from cases/amber_cipher/dimensions.json.

cold_object_examination.description: Detective alone with a single object. Cold, methodical inspection. No NPC pressure, no tell, no stance. Used for opening turns and quiet evidence beats between interviews.

first_witness_interview_cooperative.description: First contact with a witness who has no reason to lie. They give what they know plainly. The detective is questioning, the witness is open, the tell is steady. Use early in trajectory before any pressure has built.

witness_reinterview_defensive.description: Returning to a witness already questioned, this time with new evidence in hand. Their stance shifts to defensive; the body adjusts. Use mid-game, second or third pass on a witness, after a contradiction has surfaced elsewhere.

transition_pursuing_lead.description: A movement turn — the detective is in motion between locations, having just been pointed somewhere by witness or evidence. Brief, kinetic. The action is the arrival itself; the scene proper begins next turn.

dead_end_witness.description: A witness has nothing useful. They are cooperative but uninformed. The lead closes here. Used to puncture momentum and force the detective back to the evidence.

revelation_object_recognition.description: An object the detective has already seen suddenly resolves into meaning. Alone, looking at the same thing in a new light. Late investigation or closing-in beat. Pairs with name_uncovered or motive_emerges revelations.

confrontation_hostile.description: Direct accusation. The detective has the chain in hand and is putting it to the suspect. The stance is hostile, the tell is sharp, the beat is closing_in or verdict_ready. Use sparingly — once or twice per trajectory.

revisit_for_reframing.description: The detective returns to a location already visited, alone, to look at it again with the new context. Nothing dramatic — a quiet recasting of an earlier scene. Often produces a partial_match or contradiction_surfaces.

atmospheric_interlude.description: A low-activity beat. Time passes; the world breathes around the detective. Minimal scene activity, no revelation, no NPC. Used to mark act breaks, hour changes, or simply to give the prose a place to rest. One or two per trajectory.

discovery_moment.description: A find — a physical object surfaces from where it had been hidden or missed. Alone, the act of finding. Distinct from object_recognition: this is the first time the object enters the case, not the moment its meaning lands.
